pr.title: ci: run PR checks through the allowlisted main workflow

## 📌 Description

PR test jobs run from a pull-request merge ref, while the runner-group allowlist permits `pr-test.yml@refs/heads/main`. This leaves the self-hosted checks queued, as seen on #10010.

Keep `pr-test.yml` as the reusable workflow that directly defines the self-hosted test matrix and provider-spec lint. Move triggers, authorization, setup, and reporting into `pr-test-dispatch.yml`, which calls `flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/.github/workflows/pr-test.yml@main` with the selected source and matrices. The existing runner allowlist remains unchanged.

The reusable workflow independently authorizes the original event and verifies the selected source before either runner job starts. Manual dispatches outside `main` fail before setup. Both runner jobs remove only containers mounted to their exact checkout.

Reusing a prior pass requires a recorded match for PR head, current base and merge tree, including ordinary full runs and partial reruns. Legacy or expired source records require fresh CI. History refreshes every five minutes and backs off on API failures; unreadable history stays unknown.

Update scope evidence, workflow references, and nested job reporting. Preserve secrets, matrix fail-fast behavior and snapshot verification. Use the supported `github.workspace` context for the compile-cache directory.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Related: #10010 (runner scheduling investigation).

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [ ] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including the commit hooks. The full repository hook suite was not run.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).
- [ ] This PR requires **full-scope** CI, not targeted tests (expensive; justify below).
      Reason: Local workflow and CPU infrastructure checks cover this refactor; live runner admission requires the reusable interface to reach `main`.

  Suggested CI test targets (optional; paths under `tests/`, whitespace-separated — a starting
  point for `@flashinfer-bot run <targets>` / `/bot run <targets>`, reviewers may adjust): `tests/cpu/infra tests/cpu/jit/test_jit_spec_gencode_lint.py tests/infra/test_sharding`

Validation:

- actionlint passed for the reusable workflow, dispatcher, and cleanup workflow, with the organization’s custom runner labels configured; optional shellcheck was disabled.
- 116 focused CPU tests passed; workflow-only validation without `jq`: 46 passed and 6 skipped.
- Broader bot-scope and workflow tests: 67 passed, 119 subtests passed. Excluded one existing capitalization assertion (`test_target_explanations_are_sanitized_but_commands_remain_copyable`), previously reproduced on unchanged base code.
- Standards and spec reviews found no remaining code findings after fixing source inheritance for partial reruns.
- Targeted-lane scope selftest and `git diff --check` passed.

## 🔬 Experimental Track

<!-- Only for PRs submitted under the experimental policy (CONTRIBUTING.md → "Experimental APIs and Backends").
     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

- [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: #
  - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
  - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
  - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
  - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
  - [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.

<!-- Required for experimental PRs. Replace the commented lines below with your targets.
     Do not delete the fence or change its `experimental-tests` tag — the experimental-track
     watcher reads it verbatim to decide which targets to ask CI for. -->

```experimental-tests
# One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not
# supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under
# tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g.
#
#   tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py
#   tests/experimental/my_backend/
#
# Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every
# experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell.
```

## Reviewer Notes

Deployment requires the reusable `workflow_call` interface on `main` before the dispatcher invokes it. The required `Test Results Summary` check blocks ordinary pre-merge validation of the pinned call until that prerequisite is met. Stage the reusable interface first, or obtain an authorized cutover exception; this rollout finding remains open. Live runner verification follows deployment. Manual dispatches and workflow-specific API queries now use `pr-test-dispatch.yml`. The `PR Test` workflow name and required `Test Results Summary` name remain unchanged.

Implemented with AI assistance.

@@ -0,0 +1,891 @@
+# CI workflow using AWS self-hosted runners.
+# Runs AOT build tests, GPU unit tests and the CPU-only tests/cpu suite on PRs
+# to main, and on main itself on a schedule.
+# Uses ci/bash.sh for Docker execution (same as Jenkins).
+#
+# Permission Control:
+# - main: a scheduled full-suite run three times a day (not per merge). Per-merge
+#   runs shared one cancel-in-progress group, so each merge cancelled the last:
+#   about 90% of them never finished. A scheduled run is never cancelled, runs
+#   every lane to completion (no fail-fast), and a failure opens or updates a
+#   tracking issue; the next green run closes it.
+# - PRs: run when 'run-ci' or the bot's 'run-ci-focused' label is applied.
+#   Applying the label is the trigger, so new commits need a new trigger:
+#   @flashinfer-bot run.
+#
+# Instance Purchasing:
+# - All runners are on-demand. Spot was removed.
+# - A failure here is a real failure, so there is nothing to retry
+#   automatically.
+# - On-demand capacity is billed for as long as it runs, so the first failure
+#   should stop everything else. GitHub only fail-fasts within one matrix, so
+#   all tests live in a single matrix built by the setup job. They still start
+#   in parallel; the matrix exists purely to make the cancellation global.
+
+name: PR Test
+
+on:
+  # Off the 00:00 UTC nightly-release slot; one run per Asia / EU / US workday.
+  # Minute 17, not 0: GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs at the top of the hour.
+  schedule:
+    - cron: '17 4,12,20 * * *'
+  pull_request:
+    branches: [main]
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, ready_for_review]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      skip_aot:
+        description: 'Skip AOT build tests'
+        type: boolean
+        default: false
+      skip_gpu:
+        description: 'Skip GPU tests'
+        type: boolean
+        default: false
+
+concurrency:
+  # A label other than run-ci can never start tests, so it gets its own group and
+  # does not cancel - otherwise label churn would discard running GPU jobs.
+  # Scheduled runs on main get their own group and never cancel each other: at
+  # most one runs and one waits, so a slow run delays the next instead of wasting
+  # itself.
+  group: pr-test-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'scheduled-' || '' }}${{ github.ref }}${{ (github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') && '-noop' || '' }}
+  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' && !(github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') }}
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  pull-requests: write
+  statuses: read # reads the ci/test-scope status published by ci-bot-commands.yml
+  actions: read
+
+env:
+  SKIP_CI_PATTERNS: '\.md$|^docs/|^docker/|^licenses/|^LICENSE$|^NOTICE$|^benchmarks/|^\.github/CODEOWNERS$'
+
+jobs:
+  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  # Gate - Check if PR is authorized to run CI
+  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  gate:
+    name: Permission Check
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      authorized: ${{ steps.check.outputs.authorized }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Check authorization
+        id: check
+        env:
+          # Read via env, not inlined: a label name is caller-supplied text.
+          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+          EVENT_REF: ${{ github.ref }}
+          EVENT_ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
+          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
+        run: |
+          if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" != "pull_request" ]]; then
+            if [[ "$EVENT_REF" != "refs/heads/main" ]]; then
+              echo "authorized=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+              echo "::error::Select main when manually running PR Test"
+              exit 1
+            fi
+            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            echo "Main-branch scheduled/manual run, authorized"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          # Authorize on run-ci being applied, not on it being present: presence
+          # would re-authorize every later push, which is the auto-trigger this
+          # gate removes.
+          if [[ "$EVENT_ACTION" == "labeled" && ( "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci" || "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci-focused" ) ]]; then
+            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            echo "$LABEL_NAME label applied, authorized"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          echo "authorized=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "Not triggered by the run-ci label, skipping CI"
+
+  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  # Setup - Read docker tag and check if build should be skipped
+  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  setup:
+    name: Setup
+    needs: gate
+    if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      docker_tag: ${{ steps.get-tag.outputs.tag }}
+      skip_build: ${{ steps.check.outputs.skip }}
+      test_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
+      test_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.count }}
+      # Surfaced so the required check can say a green result was scoped.
+      test_scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
+      h100_disabled: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.h100_disabled }}
+      spec_lint_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_matrix }}
+      spec_lint_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_count }}
+      checkout_sha: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.checkout_sha || github.sha }}
+      snapshot_base: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_base }}
+      snapshot_tree: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      # Built here rather than written inline in the test job because the
+      # `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` publishes the requested scope as a `ci/test-scope`
+      # commit status on this SHA (see ci-bot-commands.yml). Read it verbatim - the
+      # comment was parsed once, there, and nothing is re-parsed here.
+      #
+      # Statuses come back newest-first, so the newest for this context is the last
+      # command issued. No status means nobody asked for a scope: run the full suite.
+      # Because the status is keyed to the SHA, a scope cannot outlive the commit it was
+      # requested for.
+      - name: Read requested test scope
+        id: scope
+        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
+          EVENT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
+          REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'run-ci-focused' }}
+        run: |
+          # The combined endpoint (/status, not /statuses) returns one entry per
+          # context, already the latest. Using it means re-triggering overwrites
+          # cleanly without this step deduplicating by hand, and without depending on
+          # the raw list's ordering, which is not a documented guarantee.
+          STATUSES=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/status")
+          SCOPE=$(jq -r '
+              .statuses
+              | map(select(.context | test("^ci/test-scope-[0-9]+$")))
+              | map({n: (.context | sub("^ci/test-scope-"; "") | tonumber),
+                     d: (.description // "")})
+              | sort_by(.n) | map(.d) | map(select(. != "")) | join(" ")' <<< "$STATUSES")
+          SNAPSHOT=$(jq -r '[.statuses[] | select(.context == "ci/test-snapshot")][0].description // ""' <<< "$STATUSES")
+          if [ "${REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT:-false}" = true ] && [ -z "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Automatic test snapshot was cleared or is missing. Issue a new bot run command."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
+            if [[ ! "$SNAPSHOT" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{16}$ ]]; then
+              echo "::error::Invalid automatic test snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
+              exit 1
+            fi
+            read -r SELECTED_BASE SELECTED_MERGE SELECTED_TREE SELECTED_SCOPE <<< "$SNAPSHOT"
+            ACTUAL_SCOPE=$(printf '%s' "$SCOPE" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
+            if [ "$ACTUAL_SCOPE" != "$SELECTED_SCOPE" ]; then
+              echo "::error::The automatic scope does not match its snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
+              exit 1
+            fi
+            # Reconstruct the selected source independently of GitHub's merge ref.
+            # No PR scripts, hooks, or submodule contents run during preparation.
+            for sha in "$SELECTED_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA"; do
+              git cat-file -e "${sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$sha"
+            done
+            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
+            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
+              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
+              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
+              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$HEAD_SHA"
+            ACTUAL_TREE=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
+            if [ "$ACTUAL_TREE" != "$SELECTED_TREE" ]; then
+              echo "::error::Merged source differs from AI-selected tree. Issue a new bot run command."
+              exit 1
+            fi
+            echo "Verified AI-selected tree $ACTUAL_TREE (selection $SELECTED_MERGE)"
+            echo "checkout_sha=${HEAD_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            echo "snapshot_base=${SELECTED_BASE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            echo "snapshot_tree=${SELECTED_TREE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          else
+            echo "checkout_sha=${EVENT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          fi
+          if [ -z "$SCOPE" ]; then
+            echo "No requested scope for ${HEAD_SHA}; running the full suite"
+          else
+            echo "Requested scope: ${SCOPE}"
+          fi
+          echo "test_path=${SCOPE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Validate CUDA configuration
+        run: python3 ci/validate_cuda_versions.py
+
+      # A shard script that no longer parses fails here, on the PR that changed it,
+      # instead of silently un-scheduling later targeted A10G/T4 runs.
+      - name: Validate bare-run coverage parse
+        run: |
+          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
+            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part{1,2,3,4,5}.sh
+          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \
+            --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh
+
+      - name: Get Docker Tag
+        id: get-tag
+        run: |
+          TAG=$(grep 'flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu129:' ci/docker-tags.yml | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')
+          if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Failed to extract Docker tag from ci/docker-tags.yml"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+          echo "Docker tag: $TAG"
+
+      - name: Load runtime CUDA matrix
+        id: cuda-versions
+        run: echo "runtime=$(jq -c '.runtime' ci/cuda-versions.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - name: Check Skip Conditions
+        id: check
+        run: |
+          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
+            echo "skip=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          # Use PR event SHAs for reliable diff (avoids issues with origin refs)
+          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
+          HEAD_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
+          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA")
+          # TODO (yongwww): Add back ^\.github/ before merging to main
+          SKIP_PATTERNS="$SKIP_CI_PATTERNS"
+
+          SKIP=true
+          while IFS= read -r file; do
+            if [ -n "$file" ] && ! echo "$file" | grep -qE "$SKIP_PATTERNS"; then
+              SKIP=false
+              break
+            fi
+          done <<< "$CHANGED"
+
+          echo "skip=$SKIP" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+          if [ "$SKIP" == "true" ]; then
+            echo "::notice::Skipping build - only docs/config files changed"
+          fi
+
+      # skip_aot / skip_gpu dispatch inputs have to drop entries before the
+      # matrix expands - a job-level `if` cannot see the matrix context, and
+      # skipping inside the job would still claim a runner first.
+      - name: Build Test Matrix
+        id: matrix
+        env:
+          SKIP_AOT: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_aot }}
+          SKIP_GPU: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_gpu }}
+          RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX: ${{ steps.cuda-versions.outputs.runtime }}
+          # Targets requested by the triggering `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` comment,
+          # already validated in the step above. Empty for an unparameterised run.
+          REQUESTED_TEST_PATH: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
+          H100_ON_PRS: 'true'
+          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+        run: |
+          RUN_H100=true
+          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ] && [ "$H100_ON_PRS" != "true" ]; then
+            RUN_H100=false
+            echo "::notice title=H100 lane disabled on PRs::H100 tests run only in scheduled main runs and manual workflow_dispatch runs until runner capacity is restored" >&2
+          fi
+          echo "h100_disabled=$([ "$RUN_H100" = "true" ] && echo false || echo true)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          # A targeted run on a lane never tests more than that lane's bare run: H100
+          # gets the request as-is (its bare run covers tests/); A10G and T4 get it
+          # intersected with their shard lists, and a lane left with nothing is skipped.
+          # A10G is intersected per shard: each shard whose files overlap the request
+          # runs as its own job, so a targeted run keeps the bare run's balancing and
+          # -k splits, and shards left with nothing are not scheduled.
+          A10G_SCOPES=(); T4_SCOPE=""; H100_SCOPE=""
+          if [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ] && [ -n "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}" ]; then
+            for shard in 1 2 3 4 5; do
+              A10G_SCOPES[$shard]=$(python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py \
+                --scripts "scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_part${shard}.sh" \
+                --targets "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}")
+              echo "A10G shard ${shard} targeted scope: ${A10G_SCOPES[$shard]:-<none: shard not scheduled>}"
+            done
+            T4_SCOPE=$(python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py \
+              --scripts scripts/infra/task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh \
+              --targets "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}")
+            echo "T4 targeted scope:   ${T4_SCOPE:-<none: lane not scheduled>}"
+            # tests/cpu belongs to the CPU Unittest lane, which runs on every run.
+            # The H100 lane ignores it, so drop it from the H100 scope here: a
+            # request naming only tests/cpu then schedules no H100 job instead of
+            # one that collects nothing.
+            H100_SCOPE=$(tr ' ' '\n' <<< "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}" \
+              | grep -Ev '^tests/+cpu(/|$)' | paste -sd ' ' - || true)
+            echo "H100 targeted scope: ${H100_SCOPE:-<none: lane not scheduled>}"
+          fi
+          {
+            if [ "$SKIP_AOT" != "true" ]; then
+              for arch in x64 arm64; do
+                for cuda in $(jq -r '.[].label' <<< "${RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX}"); do
+                  # Runtime entries land before their multi-arch image is
+                  # published. The release-ci-docker workflow adds the tag in
+                  # its generated follow-up PR; only then can AOT consume it.
+                  if ! grep -q "^flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-${cuda}:" ci/docker-tags.yml; then
+                    echo "::notice title=AOT image not published::Skipping ${cuda}; ci/docker-tags.yml has no published image yet" >&2
+                    continue
+                  fi
+                  jq -nc --arg arch "$arch" --arg cuda "$cuda" '{
+                    name: "AOT Build Import (\($arch), \($cuda))",
+                    kind: "aot",
+                    runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", $arch, "cpu", "on-demand"],
+                    cuda: $cuda,
+                    script: "task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh",
+                    timeout: 360
+                  }'
+                done
+              done
+            fi
+
+            # tests/cpu runs on every run, whatever scope was requested. Its
+            # tests check contracts across modules (package parity, stub
+            # configs, wrapper attributes), so a change in one directory breaks
+            # a CPU test that a scope naming that directory would not select.
+            # It needs no GPU and takes about 5 minutes on a CPU runner, and
+            # through fail-fast it stops the GPU lanes early when it fails.
+            # The GPU lanes leave it out: the H100 lane ignores tests/cpu and
+            # the A10G/T4 shard lists name no file under it.
+            if [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ]; then
+              jq -nc '{
+                name: "CPU Unittest",
+                kind: "cpu",
+                gpu_name: "CPU",
+                runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "cpu", "on-demand"],
+                cuda: "cu129",
+                script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
+                test_path: "tests/cpu",
+                timeout: 60
+              }'
+            fi
+
+            if [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ] && [ -z "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}" ]; then
+              for shard in 1 2 3 4 5; do
+                jq -nc --arg shard "$shard" '{
+                  name: "JIT Unittest \($shard) (A10G)",
+                  kind: "gpu",
+                  gpu_name: "A10G",
+                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm86", "on-demand"],
+                  cuda: "cu129",
+                  script: "task_jit_run_tests_part\($shard).sh",
+                  timeout: 360
+                }'
+              done
+
+              jq -nc '{
+                name: "JIT Unittest (T4)",
+                kind: "gpu",
+                gpu_name: "T4",
+                runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm75", "on-demand"],
+                cuda: "cu129",
+                script: "task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh",
+                timeout: 360
+              }'
+
+              if [ "$RUN_H100" = "true" ]; then
+                jq -nc '{
+                  name: "JIT Unittest (H100)",
+                  kind: "h100",
+                  gpu_name: "H100",
+                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "h100"],
+                  cuda: "cu129",
+                  script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
+                  timeout: 480

-# Uses ci/bash.sh for Docker execution (same as Jenkins).
-#
-# Permission Control:
-# - main: a scheduled full-suite run three times a day (not per merge). Per-merge
-#   runs shared one cancel-in-progress group, so each merge cancelled the last:
-#   about 90% of them never finished. A scheduled run is never cancelled, runs
-#   every lane to completion (no fail-fast), and a failure opens or updates a
-#   tracking issue; the next green run closes it.
-# - PRs: run when 'run-ci' or the bot's 'run-ci-focused' label is applied.
-#   Applying the label is the trigger, so new commits need a new trigger:
-#   @flashinfer-bot run.
-#
-# Instance Purchasing:
-# - All runners are on-demand. Spot was removed.
-# - A failure here is a real failure, so there is nothing to retry
-#   automatically.
-# - On-demand capacity is billed for as long as it runs, so the first failure
-#   should stop everything else. GitHub only fail-fasts within one matrix, so
-#   all tests live in a single matrix built by the setup job. They still start
-#   in parallel; the matrix exists purely to make the cancellation global.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Reuse CI only for a recorded head/base/tree; wait conservatively on API errors."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import io
+import json
+import os
+import re
+import subprocess
+import time
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+from urllib.parse import quote
+
+POLL_SECONDS = 300
+WORKFLOWS = {".github/workflows/pr-test.yml", ".github/workflows/pr-test-dispatch.yml"}
+
+
+class ReadError(Exception):
+    """The API has not supplied a reliable result yet."""
+
+
+def gh_api(path: str, *, binary: bool = False):
+    try:
+        result = subprocess.run(
+            ["gh", "api", path], capture_output=True, timeout=60, check=True
+        ).stdout
+        return result if binary else json.loads(result)
+    except (subprocess.SubprocessError, ValueError) as error:
+        raise ReadError("GitHub API read unavailable") from error
+
+
+class History:
+    def __init__(self, repository: str):
+        self.root = f"repos/{repository}"
+        self.sources = {}
+
+    def pages(self, path, key):
+        # Explicit pagination keeps a later burst of label events from hiding a pass.
+        page = 1
+        while True:
+            rows = gh_api(f"{path}&per_page=100&page={page}")[key]
+            yield from rows
+            if len(rows) < 100:
+                return
+            page += 1
+
+    def base_sha(self, ref):
+        return gh_api(f"{self.root}/git/ref/heads/{quote(ref, safe='/')}")["object"][
+            "sha"
+        ]
+
+    def runs(self, head):
+        return [
+            run
+            for run in self.pages(
+                f"{self.root}/actions/runs?event=pull_request&head_sha={head}",
+                "workflow_runs",
+            )
+            if run["path"].split("@")[0] in WORKFLOWS
+            and run["head_sha"] == head
+            and run["event"] == "pull_request"
+        ]
+
+    def source(self, run):
+        key = (run["id"], run["run_attempt"])
+        if key in self.sources:
+            return self.sources[key]
+        artifacts = []
+        for artifact in self.pages(
+            f"{self.root}/actions/runs/{run['id']}/artifacts?", "artifacts"
+        ):
+            match = re.fullmatch(r"pr-test-source-([1-9][0-9]*)", artifact["name"])
+            if match and int(match[1]) <= run["run_attempt"]:
+                artifacts.append((int(match[1]), artifact))
+        source = None
+        if artifacts:
+            attempt, artifact = max(artifacts, key=lambda item: item[0])
+            # Partial reruns reuse a successful authorize dependency's record.
+            # While active, a rerun of authorize may still publish a newer one.
+            if attempt < run["run_attempt"] and run["status"] != "completed":
+                return None
+            if not artifact["expired"] and artifact["size_in_bytes"] <= 16384:
+                data = gh_api(
+                    f"{self.root}/actions/artifacts/{artifact['id']}/zip", binary=True
+                )
+                try:
+                    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as archive:
+                        record = archive.getinfo("pr-test-source.json")
+                        value = (
+                            json.loads(archive.read(record))
+                            if record.file_size <= 4096
+                            else None
+                        )
+                    if isinstance(value, dict) and all(
+                        isinstance(value.get(field), str)
+                        and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", value[field])
+                        for field in ("head", "base", "tree")
+                    ):
+                        source = value
+                except (ValueError, KeyError, zipfile.BadZipFile):
+                    pass
+        # Missing artifacts can still arrive while authorization is in progress.
+        if source is not None or run["status"] == "completed":
+            self.sources[key] = source
+        return source
+
+
+def required_source(merge: str, head: str):
+    """Use the event merge's actual parents, rather than a stale PR payload base."""
+    if not all(re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", sha) for sha in (merge, head)):
+        return None
+    result = subprocess.check_output(
+        ["git", "--no-replace-objects", "show", "-s", "--format=%T%n%P", merge],
+        text=True,
+        timeout=30,
+    ).splitlines()
+    if len(result) != 2:
+        return None
+    parents = result[1].split()
+    if len(parents) != 2 or parents[1] != head:
+        return None
+    return dict(head=head, base=parents[0], tree=result[0])
+
+
+def wait_for_result(history, required, ref, current_run, *, sleep=time.sleep):
+    """A failed read is unknown; only a reliable snapshot can decide the check."""
+    delay = POLL_SECONDS
+    while True:
+        try:
+            if history.base_sha(ref) != required["base"]:
+                return False
+            runs = history.runs(required["head"])
+            active = False
+            passed = False
+            for run in runs:
+                # Older runs only: summary jobs must never wait on each other.
+                if run["id"] >= current_run and run["status"] != "completed":
+                    continue
+                if run["status"] == "completed" and run["conclusion"] != "success":
+                    continue
+                source = history.source(run)
+                if source == required and run["status"] == "completed":
+                    passed = True
+                    break
+                if run["status"] != "completed" and source in (None, required):
+                    active = True
+            if passed:
+                # The target may have advanced while history/artifacts were read.
+                return history.base_sha(ref) == required["base"]
+            if not active:
+                return False
+            print(
+                "::notice::Matching CI may still be running; checking again in 5 minutes",
+                flush=True,
+            )
+            delay = POLL_SECONDS
+        except ReadError:
+            print(
+                "::notice::CI history is unknown (API read failed); retrying",
+                flush=True,
+            )
+            delay = min(delay * 2, 3600)
+        sleep(delay)
+
+
+def main():
+    required = required_source(os.environ["GITHUB_SHA"], os.environ["HEAD_SHA"])
+    passed = required is not None and wait_for_result(
+        History(os.environ["GITHUB_REPOSITORY"]),
+        required,
+        os.environ["BASE_REF"],
+        int(os.environ["GITHUB_RUN_ID"]),
+    )
+    message = (
+        "CI passed for this PR head, current base and merge tree"
+        if passed
+        else "No verified pass for the current source. Request fresh CI with `@flashinfer-bot run`."
+    )
+    with Path(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"]).open("a") as summary:
+        summary.write(message + "\n")
+    print(message)
+    return 0 if passed else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
